rows.label: Console mode
rows.desc: Plays the game as on a docked Switch 2 (TV) or in handheld mode. The game picks its own resolution and detail for each mode.

rows.label: Fullscreen
rows.desc: Fills the screen with the game; F11 toggles it.

rows.label: Performance overlay
rows.desc: Frame rate in the top right corner. Full adds frame times with a graph, CPU, GPU and memory load, temperatures and the render thread's waits. F10 cycles the modes.

rows.label: Audio channel format
rows.desc: Speaker surround sound topology: Stereo, 5.1 Surround, or Auto-detect.

rows.label: Button layout
rows.desc: Which button is A. Nintendo: the right one, as on a Switch. Xbox: the bottom one, as labelled on an Xbox controller (cross on a PlayStation controller). Automatic picks Nintendo for controllers with Nintendo labels and Xbox for the others. Xbox prompts: A is the right one as with Nintendo, and the game shows the Xbox labels (B for A, A for B, Y for X, X for Y); the prompts change after a restart. The letters are part of the game's files, so a button you remap in Controls keeps the old letter on screen.

rows.label: Stick dead zone
rows.desc: How far a gamepad stick moves before the game sees it. Raise it if the character or the camera moves on its own.

rows.label: Menu language
rows.desc: Language of this menu and the overlay.

rows.label: GPU memory mode
rows.desc: How game memory reaches the GPU. Import: the GPU reads the game memory itself (stable). Mirror: a copy in video memory (faster, but caused crashes and flickering objects in tests).
